beats.text: Every day you say tomorrow you will change.
beats.why: Establishes the habitual promise — the audience recognizes themselves before any critique lands.
metaphorHints: calendar with tomorrow circled but never filled
word TOMORROW repeated as fading echo
unlit match held but not struck
beats.abstractMeaning: Deferred intention feels like progress while changing nothing.

timing.text: Every day you say tomorrow you will change.

beats.text: But tomorrow you repeat the same thing.
beats.why: Breaks the promise with contradiction — the loop is exposed as a self-reinforcing pattern, not a one-off slip.
metaphorHints: identical mark reappearing on the next day
closed loop of a chain or ring
struck-through word reappearing unchanged
beats.abstractMeaning: Repetition without change is the mechanism of stagnation.

timing.text: But tomorrow you repeat the same thing.

beats.text: The gap between who you are and who you want to be
beats.why: Names the central pain: distance between current self and desired self. The whole video's metaphor lives here.
metaphorHints: two silhouettes on opposite edges of a dark chasm
two profile forms separated by negative space
empty bridge span with no planks
beats.abstractMeaning: Identity distance is a physical void that can be measured and crossed.

timing.text: The gap between who you are and who you want to be

beats.why: Reframes the gap as constructed by micro-decisions — it is made, therefore it can be unmade or bridged.
metaphorHints: bridge assembling one small tile at a time
chain gaining one link per choice
staircase of small steps descending into the gap
beats.abstractMeaning: Cumulative small decisions are the building material of the gap.

beats.text: Discipline is choosing what you want most over what you want now.
beats.why: Gives the definition of discipline as a weighing act between future desire and present impulse — the core principle.
metaphorHints: balance scale where a small gold weight outweighs a large dim one
two doors: one bright-now, one gold-later
checkbox of long-term desire over immediate comfort
beats.abstractMeaning: Preference ordering: the enduring want outranks the urgent want.
beats.emphasisPhrase: want most over what you want now

timing.text: Discipline is choosing what you want most over what you want now.

beats.why: Removes both objections — timing and scale — converting principle into an achievable first act.
metaphorHints: one calendar cell fills with accent color, breaking empty days
single small point of light in darkness
first footstep mark
beats.abstractMeaning: The entry cost is near zero: now, and tiny.

beats.why: Final imperative — the entire argument collapses into one verb; hesitation is the only remaining failure.
metaphorHints: dot becoming a line, line beginning to extend
match finally struck
one step off the edge into the gap
beats.abstractMeaning: Beginning is the only action that dissolves the gap.
